messages.text: Woods set to appear in court over car crash plea

metadata.summary: Tiger Woods will appear in court for a change of plea hearing following his latest car crash earlier this year.
metadata.content: Tiger Woods: 15-time major champion set to appear in court over car crash plea | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Tiger Woods: 15-time major champion set to appear in court over car crash plea Tiger Woods was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence after he crashed his Land Rover in Florida in March; he is in court on Wednesday for a plea hearing after pleading not guilty back in April Wednesday 2 September 2026 06:48, UK Image: Tiger Woods is set to appear in court on Wednesday Tiger Woods will appear in court for a change of plea hearing following his latest car crash earlier this year. The golf legend was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence after he crashed his Land Rover in Florida in March. A police incident report said he was travelling at high speeds on a residential road when his vehicle clipped a truck during an attempted overtake and rolled on to its side. Woods had pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence in April, but the 50-year-old is set to appear in court on Wednesday for a change of plea hearing. It's not known what he will change his plea to or if he has reached a plea deal with prosecutors. The police report said deputies found two hydrocone pills - used to treat pain - in his pocket, and he showed signs of impairment. It described Woods' movements as slow and lethargic when speaking to deputies at the scene. The report also said Woods appeared to be sweating, his eyes looked glassy, and his pupils were dilated.
